title: Introduce operator-scoped audit locking, KMS tiering, and RBACv2 safelist enforcement
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Added operator-scoped audit lock to prevent duplicate audit forwards; introduced KMS tiering config and RBACv2 safelist enforcement for operator roles. Backwards compatible behind feature flags.
description: Context: Several incidents in Q4 revealed race conditions in the audit-forwarder when operator-scoped retries + multi-region KMS failover triggered duplicate audit envelopes. This PR introduces three coordinated pieces: (1) an operator-scoped audit lock that serializes audit envelope creation for operator sessions, (2) a KMS tiering policy that allows an operator to specify preferred KMS backend tiers (hot/warm/cold) and provides deterministic fallback ordering, and (3) an RBACv2 safelist enforcement for operator roles that prevents elevated operator templates from being applied to tenants with residency constraints. Motivation: reduce duplicated audit entries, make KMS failover deterministic and observable, and close a gap where operator role templates could inadvertently elevate tenant access during emergency workflows.

testing_notes: Added unit tests for lock edge cases (reentrant attempts, lease expiration) and integration tests that simulate KMS backend failures to assert deterministic fallback ordering and single audit envelope emission. E2E harness includes a 'chaos-kms' mode to simulate multi-provider timeouts.
performance_impact: Measured ~0.7% p95 tail increase on audit-write path when operator_audit_lock enabled (default off). Non-blocking fast-fail keeps tail unchanged but risks duplicate audit forward if enabled; default rollout is lock disabled -> nonblocking -> enabled with 1s timeout after 2 weeks of signals.
migration_and_rollout: Migration doc added at deploy/upgrade-migrations/2026-01-24-audit-lock.md. Rollout plan: 1) deploy feature flags to canary (2 nodes) with lock disabled, 2) enable nonblocking lock in canary, observe metrics for 48h, 3) enable full lock in canary with 1s timeout, monitor duplicate_audit_count and lock_wait_ms, 4) gradually roll to fleet over 7 days. If duplicate_audit_count rises, revert to nonblocking and investigate.
security_review: Security reviewed by Priya Nair and Ethan Cole. Threat modelling focused on denial-of-service via lock poisoning and KMS fallback amplification. Mitigations: lock lease TTL with automatic lease reclaim, bounded retry/backoff, and per-operator rate cap. RBAC safelist enforces tenant residency constraints at template apply path.
console_changes: Added feature flags 'operator_audit_lock_enabled', 'operator_audit_lock_nonblocking', and 'kms_tiering_enabled' to console feature flags UI with descriptions and suggested rollout steps. Also added RBAC safelist violation logs view under Security -> Operator Activity.
observability: New metrics: audit_lock_wait_ms{outcome=fastfail|acquired}, audit_lock_conflicts_total, kms_tier_fallbacks_total, operator_safelist_reject_total. Traces annotate lock acquisition with lock.id and operator.id for correlation.
known_issues: 1) When Redis is unavailable and nonblocking flag is off, audit writes will fall back to a local in-memory lock which does not coordinate across pods — documented and gated behind enterprise-only setting. 2) KMS tiering requires backend metadata (latency profile) to be populated by ops: missing metadata will default to declared preference order.
